title: The Council of Shirk!
summary: The editorial of al-Naba 554 attacks the establishment of a legislative assembly in post-Assad Syria under Ahmad al-Sharaa (referred to as 'al-Julani'). Its central argument is the doctrine of hakimiyya: legislation belongs to God alone, so any human legislative body constitutes polytheism (shirk) and its founders are apostates. It anchors this in Quran 12:40 and invokes Ibn Taymiyya to justify takfir of rulers who govern by other than revealed law. It cites prior guidance attributed to IS spokesman Abu Hudhayfa al-Ansari warning the people of Sham against nationalism and democracy, condemns the Muslim Brotherhood as a template for the apostasy it ascribes to the new authorities, and denounces former revolutionaries and jihadists now backing the government as supporters of a taghut. Al-Julani is framed as merely the latest in a lineage of apostate rulers.
keyClaims: Legislation is God's exclusive right, so a human legislative assembly is an act of polytheism.
Syria's new parliament under al-Sharaa is a council of shirk and its founders are apostates.
The people of Sham are being led into nationalism and democracy, betraying their sacrifices.
Former revolutionaries and jihadists now backing the government are supporters of a taghut.
significanceAssessment: This continues IS-central's doctrinal campaign to delegitimise the al-Sharaa administration, timed to the specific milestone of parliamentary formation. Framing al-Julani as the latest in a lineage of apostate rulers positions IS as the sole rejectionist alternative as Syria's transitional governance consolidates.
notes: Date converted from 17 Muharram 1448 AH. Single page (page 3) shown; editorial appears complete.
